$comment: Single source of truth for the MikePDF IPC protocol (ADR-0005). tools/MikePDF.ProtocolGen turns this into the C# and C++ codecs.
Wire format. A frame is a 4-byte little-endian body length followed by a MessagePack body of at most maxFrameBytes.
Request body:  [requestId:u64, documentId:u32, deadlineMs:u32, messageType:u16, payload:array]
Response body: [requestId:u64, status:u16, messageType:u16, payload:array|nil]  (payload is an array exactly when the status carries one)
A payload is a MessagePack array of exactly the declared fields, in key order. The key IS the array index, so keys are contiguous from 0.

Stability: a message id, a field key, a field type and an enum value are never reused or changed within a schemaVersion. Any layout change bumps schemaVersion; Hello and HelloReply keep their layout in every version so that the version check itself can always be decoded. On a mismatch the peer is killed, not accommodated.
Messages have no nesting: variable-size collections are parallel arrays tied together with sameLengthAs.
Every variable-size field has a limit and the generator rejects a schema in which any legal message cannot fit in one frame.

enums.name: Status
enums.$comment: Response status. Values with payload=true carry a reply payload, all others carry nil. Codes are master prompt 6.4. ProtocolError is also what a decoder reports for a malformed frame and InvalidArgument for a well-formed frame that breaks a schema limit.

values.name: ShellHandler
values.$comment: The native thumbnail provider or preview handler DLL in Explorer's process (docs/features/shell-extensions.md). It is only ever a client: it sends Hello to ShellHost (ADR-0018), which accepts no other kind, and no peer sends it a request. An engine refuses a Hello of this kind: the handler must never reach one.

fields.name: processKind
fields.doc: Kind of the sending process.

fields.name: pdfiumVersion
fields.doc: Empty for hosts without PDFium.

messages.name: Ping
messages.$comment: Pong carries the peer's progress counter (schema 5). It is answered by the I/O thread, so it keeps coming while the thread that does the work is busy or stuck; what moves is the counter, which that thread bumps whenever it makes progress. The broker kills an engine on a missed pong (the I/O thread is gone) or on a request that is overdue while the counter has stood still for the stall timeout (the work thread is stuck), never on a request that is merely slow while the counter moves. See docs/adr/0004 amendment A3.

fields.name: progress
fields.doc: Units of work the peer's work thread has done so far: it counts up, wraps at 2^64, and is compared for change only. 0 and a constant mean nothing happened; hosts that do all their work on the I/O thread report 0.

messages.name: AttachSlotRing
messages.$comment: Sent once, right after Hello, to an engine. The section handle is duplicated into the engine by the broker (no handle is ever inherited), so its value arrives here, not on the command line. RenderTile is refused until the ring is attached. slotCount and slotSize mirror SlotRing: at most 1024 slots (the slotIndex limit) of a multiple of 4096 bytes up to 64 MiB; the engine also checks that the section is at least slotCount x slotSize and that the total is at most 1 GiB.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: Value of the section handle duplicated into the engine, with write access.

fields.name: slotSize
fields.doc: Bytes per slot.

fields.name: handle
fields.doc: Value of the file handle duplicated into the engine.

fields.name: pdfVersion
fields.doc: Version times ten, as PDFium reports it (17 = PDF 1.7). 0 = unknown.

fields.name: permissions
fields.doc: PDF permission bits, as in the /P entry.

messages.name: GetPageSizes
messages.$comment: count is capped at 5000 so that a full reply (5000 x (5+5+1) bytes) fits one 64 KiB frame; callers page through larger documents.

fields.name: widths
fields.doc: Points.

fields.name: rotations
fields.doc: Quarter turns clockwise.

messages.name: GetOutline
messages.$comment: One level of the bookmark tree, a window of siblings at a time, so a tree is expanded lazily and a reply always fits a frame. path names the parent by the sibling index taken at each level from the root (empty = the top level); it is addressing by position, not by a handle, so it survives an engine restart. total is the number of siblings at that level (the engine stops counting at 100000). Destinations are in PDF user space of the destination page; convert with GetPageBoxes.

fields.name: path
fields.doc: Sibling index at each level, root first. At most 16 levels.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: Destination kind: 0 none, 1 page, 2 page and y, 3 page, x and y, 4 external address, 5 any other action.

fields.name: pages
fields.doc: Zero-based destination page; 0 unless kind is 1, 2 or 3.

messages.name: GetPageLinks
messages.$comment: The link annotations of one page, a window at a time. Rectangles and destinations are in PDF user space (convert with GetPageBoxes). The address of an external link is not sent here; the caller asks for it with GetLinkUri when the link is activated.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Links on the page; the engine stops counting at 100000.

fields.name: kinds
fields.doc: As GetOutlineReply.kinds.

messages.name: GetLinkUri
messages.$comment: The address behind an external link (kind 4 from GetPageLinks). Unsupported when the address is longer than 2048 bytes, is not valid UTF-8 or holds control characters; InvalidArgument when the link is not an external one.

fields.name: index
fields.doc: Position of the link in the order GetPageLinks reports.

messages.name: GetPageBoxes
messages.$comment: What the caller needs to convert PDF user space to page space (MikePDF.Core PageGeometry): the MediaBox, the CropBox when the page has one, and /Rotate in quarter turns.

fields.name: rotation
fields.doc: The page's own /Rotate in quarter turns clockwise.

messages.name: GetPageText
messages.$comment: The characters of one page in PDFium's order, a window at a time (a dense page is several replies; 2048 characters x 24 bytes fit a frame). One entry per UTF-16 code unit, with its loose box in PDF user space. The engine stops at 200000 characters and says so in truncated.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Characters on the page (at most 200000).

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: The page has more characters than the engine reports.

fields.name: units
fields.doc: UTF-16 code units.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0: PDFium made this character up (a space or line break). Bit 1: a hyphen at the end of a line.

messages.name: SearchPage
messages.$comment: Finds a phrase in one page. starts and lengths are in the character numbering of GetPageText. The engine reports at most 2048 matches per page and says so in truncated.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 match case, bit 1 whole words only.

messages.name: GetDocumentDetails
messages.$comment: What the properties dialog needs beyond GetDocumentInfo (schema 4). The two dates are the file's own text, e.g. D:20240115103000+10'00' (the broker parses them and shows what it cannot parse as text). securityRevision is the standard security handler's /R: 0 when the document is not encrypted. userPermissions is the /P the file gives an ordinary user, whoever opened the file, while GetDocumentInfoReply.permissions is what applies to this session (everything, after the owner password). formType is PDFium's: 0 none, 1 AcroForm, 2 XFA, 3 XFA foreground. Fonts are those the text on the first pages is drawn with, found by walking the page objects within a time and page budget; fontNames are printable ASCII (base font names, possibly with a subset prefix such as ABCDEF+), fontFlags bit 0 is 'embedded'. fontsComplete says every page was walked; otherwise fontPagesScanned says how many were.

fields.name: fontFlags
fields.doc: Bit 0: the font program is embedded in the file.

messages.name: GetTextQuads
messages.$comment: The quadrilaterals that mark a run of characters of one page, one per line of text, in PDF user space and in the order top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right of the text's own frame (the order Acrobat Reader and Edge expect, docs/features/text-markup.md 2.3; schema 7). start and count are in the character numbering of GetPageText; the range is cut at the end of the page's text. The engine groups characters into lines by baseline and direction, trims the whitespace at both ends of a line (a space or line break PDFium made up is never the first or last character of a quad), keeps a line-end hyphen, and reports at most 4096 quads for a range (truncated says there were more). A reply holds 64 quads (256 corners) from firstQuad on; the caller asks again with firstQuad moved on. totalQuads is the number of quads of the whole range (at most 4096). InvalidArgument: a page out of range, a start at or past the end of the page's text, or a firstQuad past the end of the quads; Damaged: the page or its text cannot be loaded.

fields.name: start
fields.doc: First character, in the numbering of GetPageText.

fields.name: count
fields.doc: Characters; the range is cut at the end of the page's text.

fields.name: totalQuads
fields.doc: Quads of the whole range, at most 4096.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: The range has more than 4096 quads; only the first 4096 are reported.

fields.name: xs
fields.doc: Four corners a quad (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), 64 quads at most.

messages.name: GetViewerPreferences
messages.$comment: The /ViewerPreferences the reader and the print dialog use (schema 5). docs/features/print.md calls it id 26, which GetDocumentDetails took in schema 4. Every value is a clamped, bounded reading of what the file says, never the raw entry: a hostile or ill-typed entry reads as absent. direction: the reading direction (/Direction), 0 left to right, 1 right to left, 2 absent. printScaling: 0 absent, 1 none (/PrintScaling /None), 2 the application default (/AppDefault). numCopies: /NumCopies from 1 to 99, 0 when absent or outside that. duplex: 0 absent, 1 simplex, 2 flip short edge, 3 flip long edge. The print page ranges are zero-based inclusive pairs (/PrintPageRange is 1-based in the file) in file order, at most 64, each first <= last and inside the document.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 annotations, bit 1 form fields, bit 2 dark pages (the tile is recoloured the way the inverted page colour does it, except for colour photographs), bit 3 the fillable-field highlight (schema 7; only with bit 1: PDFium's own form field highlight, drawn on the widgets of the page; never set for a print, a snapshot or a flattened copy). Bit 2 means printing mode in RenderBand: the two messages have their own flags.

messages.name: RenderBand
messages.$comment: A horizontal band of a page for printing (ADR-0011, docs/features/print.md 11). RenderTile stays limited to 1024 px for the viewing path; a band is as wide as the page at the printer's resolution, so it has its own limits, its own semantic checks and its own fuzz target. The page is laid out at pageWidthPx x pageHeightPx device pixels (the broker computed them from dpi, the page size and the rotation) and the band is the rows bandTop to bandTop + bandHeight of that, drawn into the slot as BGRA over white with stride 4 x pageWidthPx. The engine and the broker both check that pageWidthPx x bandHeight x 4 fits the slot and that the band lies inside the page. flags: bit 0 annotations, bit 1 form fields, bit 2 printing mode (PDFium's FPDF_PRINTING: no screen-only annotations, no LCD text). The reserved bit 3 is not allowed: max 7.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 annotations, bit 1 form fields, bit 2 printing mode.

messages.name: ListAnnotations
messages.$comment: The annotations of one page in the order of the page's /Annots array, a window of 64 at a time (schema 7, docs/features/annotation-core.md 11). The index of an entry is its position in /Annots, so a (page, index) pair names an annotation for GetAnnotation, GetInkStroke and SetAnnotationHidden. total counts every entry of /Annots, links and widgets included; the engine stops counting at 100000. An entry that is not a dictionary is reported with subtype 0 and an empty rectangle. subtypes are PDFium's FPDF_ANNOT_* values (0 unknown to 28 redact). flags are the file's /F: the engine reports the original value even for an annotation whose Hidden flag SetAnnotationHidden has set for display. Rectangles are normalised (left <= right, bottom <= top) and clamped to the schema range. colours are 0xAARRGGBB from /C with /CA as the alpha, 0 when /C is absent or when the annotation has an appearance stream (the pinned PDFium reads /C only from one that has none; GetAnnotation falls back to the first colour the stream paints with). nms is /NM, empty when absent or longer than 64 bytes. modified is the raw /M text. snippets are the start of /Contents, cut at a code point boundary. parents is the index of the annotation this one replies to (/IRT), -1 for none; it is always below total and never the entry's own index.

fields.name: total
fields.doc: Entries in the page's /Annots; the engine stops counting at 100000.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: The /F flags of the file.

fields.name: colours
fields.doc: 0xAARRGGBB; 0 when the annotation has no /C or has an appearance stream.

fields.name: nms
fields.doc: /NM; empty when absent.

fields.name: authors
fields.doc: /T, cut at a code point boundary.

fields.name: modified
fields.doc: The raw /M text; the broker parses it.

fields.name: snippets
fields.doc: The start of /Contents, cut at a code point boundary.

fields.name: parents
fields.doc: Index of the annotation this one replies to, -1 for none.

messages.name: GetAnnotation
messages.$comment: Everything the engine can read of one annotation (schema 7, annotation-core 11). index is the position in the page's /Annots as ListAnnotations reports it; an index with no dictionary there is InvalidArgument. What the pinned PDFium headers cannot read is reported as absent, not guessed: borderStyle is 0 and borderWidth is /Border's third number or 0 (the /BS dictionary is not reachable), lineEndings is empty (/LE is an array of names) and popupOpen is false (a boolean). Text values are PDF text strings decoded to UTF-8 and cut at a code point boundary at the field's limit; contentsTruncated says /Contents was cut at 16384 bytes (or was too large to read at all, and is then empty). quadPoints holds at most 64 quadrilaterals (8 numbers each) of a text markup annotation, vertices at most 1024 points (x, y pairs) of a polygon or polyline, or the two end points of a line; verticesTruncated says there were more. strokeCount and pointCount describe an ink list (strokes, and the points of all of them added up), 0 for any other subtype.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: The /F flags of the file (see ListAnnotations).

fields.name: colour
fields.doc: 0xAARRGGBB from /C and /CA (for an annotation with an appearance stream: the first colour the stream paints with, with /CA as the alpha); 0 when there is none.

fields.name: interiorColour
fields.doc: 0xAARRGGBB from /IC; 0 when absent.

fields.name: opacity
fields.doc: /CA, 1 when absent.

fields.name: borderStyle
fields.doc: Solid, dashed, beveled, inset, underline; the pinned PDFium cannot read it, so 0.

fields.name: created
fields.doc: The raw /CreationDate text.

fields.name: modified
fields.doc: The raw /M text.

fields.name: parentIndex
fields.doc: Index of the annotation this one replies to (/IRT), -1 for none.

fields.name: replyType
fields.doc: /RT: 0 none, 1 reply, 2 group.

fields.name: popupOpen
fields.doc: Always false with the pinned PDFium.

fields.name: name
fields.doc: /Name: the icon of a Text annotation or the name of a Stamp.

fields.name: lineEndings
fields.doc: Always empty with the pinned PDFium.

fields.name: defaultAppearance
fields.doc: /DA of a FreeText annotation.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: /Q: left, centred, right.

fields.name: hasAppearance
fields.doc: The dictionary has an /AP entry.

messages.name: GetInkStroke
messages.$comment: A window of the points of one stroke of an ink annotation (schema 7, annotation-core 11). stroke is the position in /InkList; first and count window its points. pointCount is the stroke's length. InvalidArgument: the annotation is not an ink annotation or has no such stroke; Unsupported: the stroke has more than 1000000 points, which the engine does not copy out of PDFium. The PDF format holds no per-point width, so hasWidths is false and widths are zeros; a later schema may carry MikePDF's private width samples (ink-pen OQ-INK-3).

fields.name: pointCount
fields.doc: Points of the whole stroke.

fields.name: widths
fields.doc: Zeros when hasWidths is false.

messages.name: SetAnnotationHidden
messages.$comment: The display mirror of the hybrid display strategy (annotation-core 3.3, schema 7): sets or clears the Hidden flag of one annotation in the engine's in-memory document, so that tiles no longer draw an original the user has deleted or moved. The engine records the file's own flags the first time it changes an annotation and gives that value back to ListAnnotations and GetAnnotation; SaveDocument restores every flag it changed before it saves, so a mirror flag never reaches a saved file (invariant 4a). hidden false puts the file's flag back. InvalidArgument: no annotation dictionary at that position.

messages.name: CountAnnotations
messages.$comment: How many user-visible annotations each of a run of pages has (schema 7, annotation-core 11), for the annotation panel's scan: every annotation except links, popups and widgets, saturating at 65535, and counting at most 100000 entries of a page's /Annots. A scan that does not finish by the deadline is Timeout with no partial result; the caller asks for fewer pages.

messages.name: GetFormFields
messages.$comment: The form widgets of the document in tab order, a window of 64 at a time (schema 7, docs/features/forms.md 10.3). total counts every widget of the document (at most 100000). Order is the pages in ascending order and, within a page, the order of /Annots: the pinned PDFium has no call that reads a page's /Tabs entry, so the row, column and structure orders cannot be told apart and every page is read in document order (forms OQ-FM-1). fieldId names a widget for GetFormFieldDetail, SetFormFieldValue and FormAction; it is the widget's position in this list and stays valid until the document is closed. types are PDFium's FPDF_FORMFIELD_* values (0 unknown, 1 push button, 2 check box, 3 radio button, 4 combo box, 5 list box, 6 text field, 7 signature). flags are the field's /Ff. states: bit 0 checked (check box, radio button) or has a selection (choice field), bit 1 has a format, keystroke, validate or calculate script (never run), bit 2 hidden (Hidden or NoView), bit 3 skipped by Tab (hidden, read-only, or entirely outside the visible box). maxLens is /MaxLen of the widget's own dictionary (0 = none or inherited from a parent field). values are the start of the field's value, empty for a password field.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: The field's /Ff.

fields.name: maxLens
fields.doc: 0 = none.

fields.name: names
fields.doc: The fully qualified field name, cut at a code point boundary.

fields.name: alternateNames
fields.doc: /TU.

fields.name: values
fields.doc: The start of the value; empty for a password field.

messages.name: GetFormFieldDetail
messages.$comment: One widget's field in full (schema 7, forms 10.3). fieldId is a position from GetFormFields. Strings are cut at a code point boundary at their limit; valueTruncated says the value was longer than 8192 bytes. defaultValue is /DV of the widget's own dictionary (a value kept on a parent field is not reachable with the pinned PDFium). maxLen is the widget's own /MaxLen, 0 when none. quadding is /Q. fontSize is the field's font size, 0 for auto. exportValue is the on-state of a check box or radio button. widgetCount is the size of the control group of a check box or radio button and 1 for every other field. optionsTotal counts the options of a choice field (at most 10000); optionLabels is a window of 64 from firstOption. The pinned PDFium reads an option's label only, so optionValues repeats the labels. selectedIndices are the selected options in ascending order (at most 64). The three has-script flags say that the widget has a format, validate or calculate action; no script is ever run. InvalidArgument: no such fieldId.

fields.name: type
fields.doc: FPDF_FORMFIELD_* as in GetFormFieldsReply.types.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: The field's /Ff.

fields.name: maxLen
fields.doc: 0 = none.

messages.name: SetFormFieldValue
messages.$comment: Changes one field's value the only way PDFium allows: through its form-fill events (focus the widget, select all, replace the selection, kill focus; a click for a check box or radio button; set-index-selected for a choice field), so the field's appearance is regenerated and its limits (/MaxLen, the choice list) are enforced by PDFium (schema 7, forms 10.3). kind 0 is text (a text field or an editable combo box; text is the new value), kind 1 is a toggle (a check box or radio button; checked is the wanted state), kind 2 is a choice (a combo or list box; selected are the wanted option positions, in ascending order, one for a combo box or a list box without the multiple-selection flag). Fields that share a name share a value, so affectedPages lists every page with a widget of the field (the widget's own first, then ascending; at most 256, with truncated set when there were more: treat every page as changed). accepted says the field now holds what was asked for; value is what it holds (the text the engine accepted, which can be shorter than asked for). PermissionDenied: the field is read-only or the document permissions (bit 9 or bit 6) forbid filling in; InvalidArgument: no such fieldId, a kind the field is not, an option out of range; Unsupported: PDFium has no form-fill environment, or the field type cannot be edited (signature, push button).

fields.name: kind
fields.doc: 0 text, 1 toggle state, 2 choice.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: More than 256 pages are affected; treat every page as changed.

messages.name: FormAction
messages.$comment: A form action the engine performs itself (schema 7, forms 3.7 and 3.8): action 0 resets one field to its default value (fieldId names a widget), action 1 resets every fillable field of the document (fieldId is ignored, send 0), action 2 activates the push button fieldId names. Only a reset is ever performed. performed: 0 nothing happened, 1 a reset was performed, 2 the button's action was refused as unsupported, 3 refused because it would send data. The pinned PDFium has no call that tells a button's action type, so the engine presses the button in a form-fill environment that has no scripting, no network and no callbacks, and reports 1 when that changed a field value and 2 otherwise; it never reports 3. affectedPages is as for SetFormFieldValue, with truncated. A reset sets a field to the /DV of its own widget dictionary or, when it has none, to empty (text and choice fields) or unchecked (check boxes and radio buttons). PermissionDenied: the document permissions forbid filling in; InvalidArgument: no such fieldId, or action 0 on a field that cannot be reset (push button, signature); Unsupported: PDFium has no form-fill environment.

fields.name: action
fields.doc: 0 reset field, 1 reset all, 2 activate button.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: More than 256 pages are affected; treat every page as changed.

messages.name: SaveDocument
messages.$comment: PDFium's own save of the engine's in-memory document into a file handle the broker duplicated into the engine, for form values and, later, page changes (schema 7, save-pipeline 3.3 stage 2 and 11.1). The engine first ends any edit in progress (kills the form focus so a typed value is committed), then restores every Hidden flag SetAnnotationHidden changed (invariant 4a), saves, and puts the display flags back so the screen does not change. mode 0 is an incremental save (FPDF_INCREMENTAL: the file's bytes are a prefix of the output, which stage 3 NormalizeTail then repairs), mode 1 a full rewrite (FPDF_NO_INCREMENTAL), mode 2 is reserved for a flattened copy and is Unsupported: ADR-0008 amendment A2 does that in the writer host (RewriteDocument). flags are the flatten options of mode 2 and must be 0 in the other modes. outputHandle is a handle value valid in the engine, with write access, to an empty file; it is closed on every path. bytesWritten is what PDFium wrote. InvalidArgument: a handle that is not a file, flags set outside mode 2; PermissionDenied: the handle cannot be written; Damaged: PDFium could not save; Timeout: the deadline had passed before the save began (a save cannot be interrupted).

fields.name: mode
fields.doc: 0 incremental, 1 full rewrite, 2 flattened (reserved, Unsupported).

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 flatten form fields, bit 1 flatten comments and markup; only with mode 2.

fields.name: outputHandle
fields.doc: A write handle valid in the engine, to an empty file.

messages.name: ValidateStructure
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only. 256 issues of at most 192 message bytes fit one frame (512-byte messages would not).

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: More issues were found than fit.

messages.name: AppendAnnotations
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only (schema 6, save-pipeline 3.3 stage 4). Appends one incremental update for the annotation edits in the edit blob (save-pipeline 11.3: a second format, MessagePack, read from editsHandle; not a frame) to the base document and writes base plus update to outputHandle. Every file is a handle duplicated into the host: baseHandle and editsHandle are read-only, outputHandle has write access and is empty. pageCount is the base's page count the edits were made against; a different count is InvalidArgument. A status other than Ok carries no payload, so a refusal the broker needs the reason for is an Ok reply with ok false and issueCodes (PdfErrorCode) and issueMessages in the shape of ValidateStructureReply: the strict parser refuses the base, the base is encrypted or over a limit, the page count differs, an edit's expectation does not hold. InvalidArgument: a handle that is not a file, an edits length that is not the file's, a blob that does not decode. Timeout and PermissionDenied as for ValidateStructure.

fields.name: editsLength
fields.doc: The blob's length in bytes, at most 256 MiB.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: More issues were found than fit.

messages.name: NormalizeTail
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only (schema 7, save-pipeline 3.3 stage 3, ADR-0008 decision 3 step 3, S11 report). Repairs the tail PDFium appended to a file in its incremental save. originalHandle is the file as it was opened, pdfiumHandle the engine's SaveDocument output (mode 0: the original's bytes, then PDFium's update), outputHandle an empty file; all three are file handles duplicated into the host, the first two read-only. The host parses the original strictly, checks that the PDFium file starts with the original's exact bytes, reads the objects PDFium appended and writes the original's bytes followed by those objects and a new cross-reference section in the same form as the original's newest section (a table after a table, a stream after a stream with its own entry), with /Prev, /Size, /Root, /Info and a trailer /ID that keeps the first element. flags: bit 0 restore the original check box and radio button state streams for widgets whose state names are unchanged (forms 10.2, keeping PDFium's /AS and /V), bit 1 remove PDFium's private keys (/PDFIUM_HasGeneratedAP). A refusal with a reason is an Ok reply with ok false and issues in the shape of ValidateStructureReply, as for AppendAnnotations: the strict parser refuses the original, the PDFium file does not begin with the original, the appended part is ambiguous (a duplicate key, an object it cannot read). InvalidArgument: a handle that is not a file; Timeout and PermissionDenied as for ValidateStructure.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 restore author check box and radio state streams, bit 1 strip PDFium private keys.

fields.name: truncated
fields.doc: More issues were found than fit.

messages.name: RewriteDocument
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only (schema 6, save-pipeline 3.3): a full rewrite of the base into outputHandle, for Save As 'Rewrite the whole file' and for a flattened copy. flags: bit 0 draw form fields into the pages and remove them, bit 1 draw comments and markup into the pages and remove them (max 3). The output holds only what the catalog can reach: no older revision, no flattened annotation. Handles as for AppendAnnotations. The reply says what was done; ok is false with issues as for AppendAnnotations, and the statuses are as there.

messages.name: VerifyAnnotations
messages.$comment: MikePDF.WriterHost only (schema 6, save-pipeline 3.3 stage 5): a second, independent strict parse of the base and of a finished output. It checks that the output has pageCount pages and that, for each page named in pages, the number of annotations that are not links, popups or widgets is the base's number plus added minus removed, where added and removed are the broker's model (what the edits say). mismatches lists the pages (from pages) whose count differs. The broker sends at most 2048 pages per call and calls again for more. Both handles are read-only and valid in the host.

fields.name: ok
fields.doc: Both files parse strictly and the output has pageCount pages.

messages.name: ShellOpen
messages.$comment: MikePDF.ShellHost only (schema 5, ADR-0018, spike S6b section 'Protocol: messages and schema v5'): the first message a thumbnail provider or preview handler DLL (ProcessKind ShellHandler) sends on its pipe after Hello. The connection is the session. Handle direction: section is a handle value valid in the SENDING process (the handler), with read access; ShellHost duplicates it from the process at the other end of the pipe (GetNamedPipeClientProcessId, then DuplicateHandle), which a handler running at Low integrity can still allow. bytes is the file size (the section may be larger). There is no password: a shell never prompts. The reply's documentId is the session, and every later message of the session carries it in the envelope.

fields.name: section
fields.doc: A section handle valid in the handler (the sender), read access.

fields.name: bytes
fields.doc: The file size, at most 32 MiB.

fields.name: documentId
fields.doc: The session: the envelope documentId of ShellRenderPage and ShellClose.

fields.name: firstWidth
fields.doc: Points.

fields.name: firstHeight
fields.doc: Points.

messages.name: ShellRenderPage
messages.$comment: Renders one page to fit maxWidth x maxHeight (16 to 1024: the tile limit, to be raised when a band message serves the shell) into a section the handler made. pixels is a section handle valid in the SENDING process (the handler) with write access, duplicated by ShellHost the same way as ShellOpen.section; pixelBytes is at least maxWidth x maxHeight x 4 (the handler's check, repeated by ShellHost against the section). flags: bit 0 draw annotations, nothing else (max 1). The pixels are in the caller's section. The reply values the schema cannot tie to the request, and which the handler must check before it builds a bitmap: width <= maxWidth, height <= maxHeight, stride == 4 x width.

fields.name: flags
fields.doc: Bit 0 annotations.

fields.name: pixels
fields.doc: A section handle valid in the handler (the sender), write access.

fields.name: stride
fields.doc: Equal to 4 x width.

messages.name: ShellClose
messages.$comment: Optional: closing the pipe ends the session just the same.
